text: On the Origin of Species by Charles Darwin was banned from Trinity College, Cambridge, England, in 1859. In 1925 Tennessee enacted the Butler Act, which made it illegal for schools to teach content that conflicted with the Book of Genesis, and a source describes the book by Darwin as banned under it.

sources.title: Book censorship in the United States (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: The Butler Act , enacted in Tennessee in 1925, made it illegal for schools to teach content that conflicted with the Book of Genesis

note: Butler Act restricted teaching of evolution; source (Wikipedia) frames it as the book being banned. Reviewer may prefer to drop.

text: Random House cancelled the 2008 release of The Jewel of Medina by Sherry Jones over concerns about possible inflammatory content. After the novel appeared in Serbia in August 2008, the Serbian publisher Beobook withdrew it from stores following strong reactions from the Serbian Muslim community, then returned it to shelves shortly after. The government banned The Jewel of Medina in Malaysia in 2009.

sources.title: The Jewel of Medina (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: Although the novel was originally scheduled for release in 2008 by Random House , it was cancelled due to concerns about possible inflammatory content.

sources.title: The Jewel of Medina (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: After strong reactions from the Serbian Muslim community , Serbian publisher Beobook withdrew it from stores

note: Random House cancellation and Beobook withdrawal were publisher actions, not government bans.

text: Candy by Terry Southern and Mason Hoffenberg was banned by the Paris vice squad after Olympia published it in October 1958. The Indecent Publications Tribunal banned Candy in New Zealand in 1969 after ruling it indecent.

sources.title: Terry Southern (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: published in UK Harper's Bazaar in August 1958. In October, Olympia published Candy under the pseudonym Maxwell Kenton, and it immediately was banned by the Paris vice squad.

note: Existing China 2003 ban row refers to Mian Mian's different novel Candy, not this book; flag.
